slot_note: seed ET35 (repeat-disaster counties across a FEMA region): the world screened at the draw and set aside (every unobserved quantity it offers is a spent lane mechanism and the declaration count itself is records-fixed, its levers 'Statewide' rows, amendments and spellings data semantics); the decision kept in form (which administrative areas a programme serves, on a count per area) in a fresh world: a state DOT district's spring patching crews placed by the potholes its camera-equipped maintenance fleet found and did not find in a March detection campaign
niche: a state DOT district's count of the distinct potholes its camera-equipped maintenance fleet recorded on each maintenance section's state roadway in March, resolved from raw detections that each phone places ahead of the pothole by its own GPS latency in its direction of travel, placing its spring patching crews
answer: Give dedicated spring patching crews to seven of the fourteen sections: Elmscourt, Thistlebank, Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Norvelle, Kestrelton and Fenwick Gap.
answer_source: submission.md block 1; generator/figures.json call.designated and sections.*.rate
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms Kerbline's detections, the telematics traversals, the road inventory and its crosswalk and reads every rule correctly links the detections into potholes at one distance and designates five sections at anything from 132 to 410 feet (Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle) or a seven with Grisholt and Oxbrae for Fenwick Gap and Kestrelton at 54 to 124 feet; checked on the surveyed utility covers the error is centred on zero at a median of 53 feet, which reads as scatter, and a tolerance per unit from it designates the five again; only each detection moved back by its unit's latency at its own pass's direction and speed designates the seven.
domain_test: General statistics, so the swap is of the method: the deciding quantity is a count of distinct entities resolved from position reports that carry a systematic, direction-dependent instrument bias, the bias calibrated per instrument on control objects of surveyed position and removed using each report's own direction and speed before the reports are linked; a generic dedup at one distance designates other sections at every distance, and without the surveyed controls and the pass record the bias cannot be measured or removed.

driver: Distinct entities are counted from position reports that each instrument displaces along its direction of travel by its own latency times its speed, so one entity seen in both directions appears as two tight clusters; the latency is calibrated on control objects of surveyed position and each report corrected by its pass's direction and speed before linking, while any single linking distance either splits the two directions or merges close neighbours.
driver_concrete: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles counts the distinct potholes its Kerbline detections resolve to after each detection is moved back along its pass by its unit's GPS latency (measured against the asset inventory's surveyed utility covers) times the pass's speed from the telematics traversals, because every phone places what it sees ahead of where it is, northbound to the north and southbound to the south.
stump: The default path links the pothole detections at one distance and designates Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle at anything from 132 to 410 feet, or a seven with Grisholt and Oxbrae at 54 to 124 feet, because every Kerbline phone places a detection ahead of the pothole along its direction of travel by its own GPS latency times its speed, so on the two-lane roads one pothole seen both ways is two clusters while the bridge decks' neighbouring potholes sit closer than that; each detection moved back by its unit's latency on the surveyed covers at its own pass's speed and direction, the detections designate the seven.

lineage.driver: Each section's potholes per ten lane-miles in March 2027 counts the potholes no camera unit recorded, completed segment by segment as one over the chance that at least one of the distinct installed units that drove the segment found a pothole, the per-unit chance (0.542) read from how often a second unit found a pothole another unit found; a unit records the same potholes on every pass (99.5 per cent of its later days), so a segment its section's patrol pickup drove on seven or more days has had one chance.
lineage.stump: The default path completes the potholes no unit recorded by treating every pass over a segment as an independent chance at the rate a pass re-finds a found pothole (64 per cent of unit-days), which changes nothing on segments driven seven or more times, and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt only; the rural and outer suburban sections one unit drove hide close to half their potholes, and Fenwick Gap, Thistlebank, Holloway Run, Kestrelton and Norvelle clear the line at 7.08 to 8.29.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: reader G (the ninth isolated reader) landed the call by distinct-unit capture-recapture; readers C to H kept ask A's counts and two kept the camera miles

lineage.driver: Distinct entities are counted from repeated positional reports by instruments of unequal accuracy, each instrument's error measured on surveyed control objects, so reports are linked within a tolerance that follows the instrument; any single tolerance either splits a noisy instrument's reports of one entity or merges an accurate instrument's reports of distinct neighbours.
lineage.stump: The default path links the pothole detections into potholes with one milepost tolerance for every unit and designates another set at any tolerance it picks; the street sweepers' older Kerbline units place their reports of one pothole tens of feet apart while the patrol units' reports of neighbouring bridge-deck potholes sit a few yards apart, so only a tolerance set by each unit's error on the surveyed utility covers resolves both.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 on 2026-10-21: readers C and D landed the call by folding the sweepers' visibly scattered reports into the precise units' potholes; the camera miles ask leaked to both round 1 readers and was dropped

lineage.driver: A count seen through several instruments is completed by multiple-list recapture, and instruments of one family see the same members while different families see independently, so the occasions are the distinct families that looked at a unit at the cross-family recapture rate, not the instruments; taking every instrument as independent overstates the find rate and completes too little.
lineage.stump: The default path completes pass by pass and designates Carrow Point and Elmscourt; the careful path takes every installed unit as an independent chance at 69.9 per cent and designates five; units of one fleet group record 93.6 per cent of each other's potholes against 54.9 per cent across groups, so the chances are the fleet groups at 54.4 per cent, and Fenwick Gap (6.86) and Kestrelton (7.28) join Holloway Run, Carrow Point, Elmscourt, Thistlebank and Norvelle.
